findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 1df45564178ed5b0d1207a512c881136b9e568e0e6cacf4d6fe712df5c8e8f30; all 4 declared sources passed current HTTPS access review.

The official plan PDF was retrieved at 971,223 bytes with SHA-256 c95d84641a0d024c04b9d8ba491e5972085b29a05a9aba4038128d78e8e12d01; it is unencrypted, has no JavaScript, contains 75 physical pages, and records creation on 2024-08-08 and modification on 2024-09-02.

Physical page 42 says mineral properties are identified and appraised based on an RRCID, production before an RRCID may be reported by drilling permit number, and beginning-of-year searches cover new wells that started producing before January 1.
Physical page 42 prints three January 1 conditions: reported production, a completion report showing completion, or perforation into a producing formation showing oil or gas before January 1.

Physical pages 42-43 describe completion reports and plats for location, jurisdictional-map cross-checks for situs, DOI requests for working and royalty interests, later database reviews, and supplementation going back up to five years.
Current RRC pages use API, drilling permit, lease ID, gas ID, and form labels. The article preserves rather than silently reconciles that terminology with the plan term RRCID.
